tips.comment: Price seems about right. Has placed third and second in handicaps recently. Just needs to continue that improvement and should be winning this race. 7/2 and 100/30 recently.

Always A Reason is a 6-year-old gelding trained by Rebecca Menzies and ridden by Ross Chapman, who make a good team with 29/193 wins, showing a LSP of £8.18. Always A Reason is a PTP winner and hasn't shown a great deal in three events, posting a career-high RPR of 88. He makes his handicap hurdle debut today off 93, so the handicapper is taking no chances, but it's still a lowly rating. Always A Reason is definitely one to consider in this weak-looking contest.
He is a dual course winner over 2m, and he is just 1lb higher than the most recent of those wins. But this mark is still attainable as he is 8lbs lower than his Kelso win in a class 2.

Cage Rattler was a modest winner on the flat over seven furlongs at Gowran in May 2024. Now only rated 44, he has been priced at 100-1 or above in all four of his hurdle races so far. Last time, in his first handicap at Newcastle, moved up to a similar distance, he was going nowhere at the back until the home straight. Then he made rapid progress between the final two flights to close on the leaders but could find no more on the run-in, finishing 3rd at 100-1. He may be more suited to the undulations of Hexham and could win off the same mark.

Noble Affair won over CD two years ago, and despite a close 2nd after that, she has been in the doldrums until last start 42 days ago at Ayr 2m4f soft when running her best race for a while under today's rider, without the 5lb claim that he gets today. If building on that run, then off today's weights, she is capable of being there at the finish.

Romeo Brown is one I've been following, and to me, hasn't run as bad as the figures suggest. But meanwhile, its mark has plummeted, and it finds itself in a class 5 here and has had the magic wind op! One more go.

Showed some promise on the flat in 2023 and over hurdles last year. Good 2nd at Carlisle in October over 2m 1f. Staying on that day, just held. Another couple of decent efforts after, and although 6th last time out, might have needed a run and stronger race than this one. Open race this and worth another shot at this longer trip.
Showed some promise on last outing. Gets better ground today, which should suit. Makes handicap debut off a good mark. Trip shouldn't be a problem. Can run a big race.

He'd had 3 good runs with a 3rd and 1st here including over course and distance and a 3rd at Sedgefield before disappointing last time out at Catterick. That can be excused as the 3m2f trip was too far and he returns to the course and distance of his last win.

Aquitaine Boy won a C5 back in January off a 95 and has not been so good for the last two runs in C4. But he has dropped to a 98 and gets back to C5 today, so he could be back in the game after a run to second with Brian last time out.

Tan Law is still lightly raced and caught the eye when stepping up in trip from 2 miles to 3m3f at Sedgefield, travelling well before fading before the final hurdle. He backed that up with an improved performance last time out at Bangor, chasing home the progressive Richardson on testing ground in a race where many struggled to finish. I suspect today's better ground could suit him, and with another 4lb drop in the weights for what was a decent effort, he looks worth an each-way bet over this intermediate trip.

It's Dan. He remains a maiden but has had two 2nd places, including last time at Ayr when he faded after a mistake at the last on his first run since wind surgery. Dropped another pound to his lowest mark of 95, he could break his maiden tag.
Entered veteran territory, but legs seem to still be competitive and notched up two good runs at Musselburgh last month. Still lighter than in last win and has won at this distance.
Maillot Blanc actually does surprisingly well here at this track and won't mind the better ground that is on offer here. Great each way chance.
It's a value price considering it won well last time out. More to come here in a weak-looking race with conditions that will favor the horse.

This is a mediocre race with little to recommend any of them, but this lad is at least unexposed and ran encouragingly last time out. He returned from a break to be pulled up after 5 flights at Newcastle after the saddle slipped, so in effect, this is his second run of his season. Two weeks ago, he finished well over an inadequate 2 miles here, and we can expect a bolder show today over a juicy low weight.

Santa Clarita was pulled up on penultimate start before showing better signs of form last time in a Class 4 handicap at Ayr, 2m5f, good to soft. In the three runs prior to those starts, he had been 2nd twice in Class 4 handicaps. Today's race is not as strong as his last start, and the drying ground could well help him at the finish today. If building on that last effort, then the 7-year-old has place claims at least in this.
Has an obvious chance. Was third LTO, and the second has since won. Had excuses there too, could have finished closer. Winner is useful.

He's far from reliable, but KINGSTON ROCK is very exposed over hurdles. However, he had his best run yet over this course and distance two weeks ago. With his regular jockey claiming 5lb, he has a fair chance of making the places. The market is heavily biased towards the favorite, Road To Home, Willie Mullins' only runner today, but his form doesn't look anything startling considering the current odds.
Good run recently at Newcastle when he stayed on well. Ground and trip fine, and perhaps more improvement in him than others. He should go close.
Placed 2nd last time out, and hopefully delivers a promising performance this time. Has shown course and distance success with a hint of experience on going.
He does have a win and 4 places efforts at this track, and although making his first run over fences since March 2022, when finishing 3rd at this track over 4m, he is now 19lbs lower than that today.

Beat The Boum could be a chip off his block sire, Bucks Boum, who is by Cadoudal. Al Boum Photo franked the bloodline by winning the Gold Cup back in the day. Beat The Boum is now going chasing, which may see him being capable of staying in touch, with the gallop being a stride or so less than over hurdles. After seven outings without winning, Jackie Stephen might have this race in mind for jockey Danny McMenamin to get his mount jumping soundly, with him powering to the line for success.
The favorite can't be relied on to back up the win as it hasn't done in the past. This one won a PTP and had average hurdles form but might be better over fences.
Maggs takes off 5 lbs, which will be a big help. Has held his form well recently and C&D to suit.
Rewired dropped to C4 company last time out and won off a 107 by over 3L. Only up 4 lbs, so could be in with a chance of a double while staying in C4.
Lawrenny has been very consistent so far. Hoping there is a lot more as this is competitive, but it has done everything right to step up again. Sean Quinlan is the equalizer here, so fingers crossed.

Just three runs over the winter for the 6yo and he made a winning handicap debut last time out. He travelled well in that 13 runner contest and found plenty at the business end of the race. Four of the well beaten runners in that race have run well since, so the form looks solid. Only a slightly higher mark now, will be fresh after a six week break and can have more to offer.

Not the most reliable horse you'll see, but has now dropped back to what looks like a nice enough mark with a nice racing weight, with the jockey taking off 7 lbs also. He's still fairly lightly raced over hurdles, just 7 runs to date. He managed to win on hurdling debut, winning over CD with any amount in hand, beating Max Of Stars by 8L. He finished 2nd in his next 2 hurdling runs, with Max Of Stars reversing that form at Newton Abbot NTO. He then bumped into Myristica at Stratford on his next run. He's not shown much in his 4 hurdling runs since, a combination of soft ground and hard luck stories (unseated rider twice). In his most recent run, he probably didn't stay that trip. His rider lost irons briefly too. He drops back to the correct trip this time, running on his preferred faster ground. He's won here before, so that's a nice positive.

Is a fair hurdler on his day and having fallen at Carlisle four starts ago was given a considerate ride next time at Ayr, probably to restore confidence, and finished a never nearer 5th over two miles. Was kept to that trip next time at Haydock but failed to get involved albeit in a much tougher race. Appeared unsuited by the step up in trip last time so can get back on track here, back at two miles.

He enjoys this track having won over course and distance and placed on multiple occasions. Despite being a maiden over fences, he is on the same mark as his hurdles win at this track, and he was a very good 2nd last time out. He finished a half length behind Divas Doyen but is now 8lbs better off with that winner and should turn the tables for how short the margin of victory was last time out.
Choose A Copper seems to like it here at Hexham and looks to still have a bit of wiggle room in the chasing development space for a yard going great guns. Worth a bet here.
Was very impressed with Divas Doyen's last run LTO and still being at a handy mark. Miss Heidi Palin gives us a 7lb claim too, which should help a lot. 8/1 is great value here.

In what looks like a very tricky-looking race, I'd be quite keen to take on the current market leader 'Halpha Soleil'. One that catches my eye back on today's better ground is this inmate of the M. Todhunter yard, who has dropped back into Class 4 company for the first time in a while and has been running with credit over further. It is interesting that the last time he ran in Class 4 company, he beat 'Donny Boy' by a head at Newcastle (2m 7f 91yds) on good ground back in December 2023 and is only 3lb higher today.
11 years old now but still has talent. Dropped in class and trip which will suit him a lot more. Handicap mark has also plummeted.
Trac has not been great since the break last November but has dropped to that last winning C2 mark. It could find this drop to C4 a tad easier now, having had wind surgery. EW
Most experienced horse in the field. First time running with a tongue strap and claiming less weight with Jack Power on board.

There doesn't look to be much between the odds-on favorite and Nseventeen, who is 11/2. The selection has got a nice pedigree, being by Idaho, who is beginning to make a name for himself as a National Hunt sire. His Irish Point-to-Point form looks very decent, with a number of the horses in that race performing very well since.
Brother to Hidden History looks bred for the job, and the trainer can ready one. Also, the race looks winnable for a debut runner.

He is a half brother to Put the Kettle On and Listed bumper runner up Carningli. That is a very strong pedigree and the fact the favourite has been 5/1 or less in all 3 of his starts and is yet to win could mean that he doesn't win again at shorter than 5/1.

Eagles Cairn is open to lots of improvement having finished 3rd last month at Carlisle, but not given a hard ride once the jockey knew the nap was not going to win that contest. More is expected today.
Second outing since his wind surgery, which seemed to have worked. Now on his second time out, hoping to repeat history.

Rated mid-70s on the flat and wasn't done with in that sphere, so potentially thrown in off today's mark if improving for those recent efforts. Obviously, the favorite from Nicholls' yard, respect it, but don't overlook this one.
Backed like defeat out of the question last time. Was 13/8 fav, only 5th. Still a maiden but not had much racing. Has ability, clearly just needs to click. Lower handicap mark today will help.
Benefits from a 7lb allowance, improving recent performances, and conditions that suit. Faces a winnable field, making her a good value selection.

Both runs this year have been on left-handed tracks, and her last win came on a right-handed track like Taunton when winning at Market Rasen in June 2024. Just the 4 races since, and she will be fitter for 2 runs in 2025 following a 200-day absence. The return to a right-handed track could inspire.

Banny Hill Lass has had three bumper runs and three runs over hurdles, all at big prices and shown little but this mare steps up in trip on handicap debut from a lowly opening mark. Last couple of runs she was well beaten but was up against some fairly decent types, both winners are rated 122 and 137, whereas she starts off here from a mark of 74, so should find this task much easier.

A greater test of stamina amongst her own sex may help Sawpit Samantha enjoy her racing. She's shown potential over shorter. The booking of jockey Gavin Sheehan catches the eye and she looks interesting in the terms of this handicap.

Both Zucayan's wins have come at Ludlow over two miles on good going but he still looks competitively handicapped on his mark of 99 and Nick Slatter who has ridden him in all 18 of his races rides him again at Taunton.

Typical when you fancy one in a race you find another, and that's what has happened here. I think the Michael Blake runner off such a low weight will be competitive, but have decided to go with Taritino who ran a race full of promise 15 days ago in a higher grade than this. Has never won over hurdles in 8 starts, but is here off a career low mark and 2lb lower than his last race here earlier this month. Will love the ground and I can see him going close and defy his odds.

It's been just over two years since John Betjeman last entered the winner's enclosure. That was a two-mile hurdle race at Ffos Las when racing off a mark of one hundred and nine. Following an encouraging run at Wincanton earlier this month where he finished second, his rating for today is ninety-seven. Fergus Gillard is back on board, and if John Betjeman can build on that encouraging run, then there are possibilities of gaining the win.

A Daisy Hitchins trained 9-year-old who has had 20 races over the hurdles, winning 3 times and has finished in the frame 9 times. His last win was in October last year in a class 5 handicap hurdle at Stratford over 2m 2 1/2f on heavy going, ridden by today's jockey Mr. Robbie David claiming 7 lbs when beating the favorite by 1 1/4 lengths. His last 4 races have been over the bigger obstacles and he is reverting back to the hurdles in this class 5 handicap hurdle over 2m 1/2f on good going. This gelding has won 4 times over the chases and has won 3 times over the hurdles and has won over this distance. He has been keeping his form well. Has a decent e/w shout in this race today.
Used to be with Henderson and has now become well handicapped, has back class and is not done improving just yet. Could easily take this
Very consistent type and I think at these odds bigz belief is worth it here, 5lb claim and progressive form could really Outrun the odds.

This is probably the last type of bet I should be with on current form, but I just think this is a pretty weak race. Maybe PRINCE RHINEGOLD, even though from an unfashionable stable, drops to a workable mark and also drops in grade here. Has each-way claims as could potentially pick off a few of these if running in a similar vein to the showing at Wincanton the run before last.

Us and Them, a sprightly 12-year-old, goes at Taunton for the very first time. Yet I've read its breeding suggests this is the track that gets the results with a 44% strike. Now, it can't be improving, but just maybe it can place where at one bookie you can still get 66/1 for five places.
Came 2nd last time out in Taunton. This time we have better going and an extra 2 furlongs, which shouldn't hinder too badly.

Connections may have found Edeiffs Rock a nice race to get another win. This is competitive but took down a similar race in February fairly comfortably. Only 5 runs over fences, so there is clearly potential for more. Hoping this is ridden near the front as it definitely looked to suit.
Won LTO and gets the chance to go back to back. Most of these have strong form coming into the race. This one can potentially still improve a bit for the trip.

Looks a very winnable race, and though upped in grade, this one comes here in form and looks ready to strike for his in-form yard. Finished well clear of the rest in 2nd last time. The one to be on here.

Relishes decent ground and should build on the C&D win before Christmas when beating a useful sort from Seven Barrows. Just 4lbs higher here back in a class 4 and should be more to come over this trip.
This Henderson runner is yet to show true form. For sure, there is something to come, having only run twice for the stable and was highly tried last time out. It should come good soon.
Wouldn't completely rule it out. Has won two of its last six starts overall. Becoming well handicapped and the course and distance will suit. Jockey going well.
Pulled up the last twice. If jumping better, should go well. Was third before that, and this race is no tougher. Room for improvement too.
Bobbi's Beauty looks to be the best pick in this field with the brilliant Sean Bowen onboard. Has got the form in here that will blow the others out of the water.
Recently received a wind operation and was quite prominent in running. If luck prevails, K.O.T.L should steer into success with a smaller field.
80/1 on debut, finished 3rd in a big field. Switched to Nicholls' yard since and ran okay last time. Sets the standard here.

Ana Emaraaty returns to the AW just 1lb above his last winning mark and shaped well on his latest start at Newcastle, finishing second after being held up off a steady pace. He’s two from five at the track, and both wins came under similar race conditions. The booking of Rossa Ryan catches the eye, and the yard has a solid record with runners fresh. With a decent pace likely this time, he should get the race run to suit and looks a fair price to go close.
Keeps improving and won in another career-best effort last time in the style of one that the handicapper hasn't got to grips with yet. Down in trip is my only concern in a race with no pace.

Hijo De La Luna looks interesting at Newcastle. His speed ratings are pretty good, and the drop back to 1m2f should suit him better after he seemed to struggle a bit over 1m4f last time. The cheekpieces are back on, which have helped him in the past. At the odds, he could be worth an each-way flutter

I must be a total thickhead because I wouldn't back the current favorite in this race even if it was a free bet and I was guaranteed a place in heaven, which I believe is getting a tax rebate and having to wait for the toilet. Three Yorkshiremen would not drag me there. My selection is Made All, who has run a lot better and seems to be coming along nicely in recent outings. At this price, it is not a certainty but looks better than most.
Won in December over a trip he likes and gets the return of a useful jockey today. Should do much better than last time and CD to suit.
Went well when second last time out. I wouldn't say this is much tougher, and we still believe it's going to run a big race today with top weight.

Course and distance winner, beaten favorite last time when a head second and one pound better off with that horse this time. Jockey in good form, should be given serious consideration. Nap each way at 8/1.

Violeta runs in the 5:15 at Newcastle and has two career wins to her name, both of which came over this course and distance, so she clearly enjoys the track. She’s not the most consistent, but she’s shown she can pop up when conditions suit. This doesn’t look like a strong race and returning to a venue that brings out the best in her gives her a bit of an edge.
Alex the Great should still be able to get up off this mark. Clear standout in this field for me, CD form and still very progressive.

Trainer James Owen is building up a fine reputation when it comes to turning around the fortunes of horses that have been out of sorts with their previous trainers. Market House finished 3rd on his debut for the stable, then won 2 on the bounce and on just his 4th run is seeking the hat-trick this evening. The step up in trip shouldn't be a problem for the former hurdler, and he should prove hard to beat.

Val Bassett has already proven he stays this trip and actually won over course and distance last autumn, so the return here is a big plus. He flopped a bit last time out, but he’s got that bounce-back vibe and isn’t badly treated on old form.
Might be the one to be with. Finished second LTO. That was a return to form and has gone well over this C&D in the past. Also knows how to win races.

Useful mare hasn't won for almost 30 months and has become inconsistent. However, she showed she retains ability when just failing to get up over this course and distance in January. Fair effort subsequently at Wolverhampton but has been disappointing the last twice. Remains competitive off current lowly mark, and if on a going day looks capable of springing a surprise.

Turquino is unbeaten on debut at Southwell over 11.1f, despite being slowly away. Proven on Tapeta and expected to improve. He's the one to beat given his profile and trainer form. He sets the standard and should confirm his strong debut impression.
Does get weight off the market leaders and isn't out of this. Improved on debut run when 4th LTO and can continue that progress here.

Destination Unknown lines up in the 6:15 at Newcastle making his debut over 1m4f. While there’s no form to go on, the yard is going along nicely, and that always adds a bit of interest. He’s a half-brother to Metier, so there’s stamina and ability in the pedigree. This trip on debut suggests he might be more of a staying type. Hard to know what to expect, but he’s not the worst shout for a speculative play.

Just Typical shaped nicely on debut over this C&D when third behind a pair that had experience, showing good early pace before tiring late. That run came after a gelding op, and he should come on plenty for it. The yard has a strong record with second-time starters, and the switch to cheekpieces suggests intent. With natural improvement, he should be competitive, and in a field lacking depth, he looks a fair price to step forward.

Wyvern is a course and distance winner and ran well here last time out when beaten less than a length. He doesn't win often and is not a confident selection, but he was favored last time and expected to do well. Maybe today is when he puts it all together. The trainer has had no winners from 13 runners, but 5 of them were placed, so he has been knocking on the door.

Drakeholes is back at the scene of two strong wins late last year. He clearly likes this track and trip, and now that he’s had a couple of runs to blow off the cobwebs, there’s a chance he could bounce back in a big way. It’s a bit of a roll of the dice, but he’s done the job here before and that makes him dangerous to ignore in this sort of field.
Has been behind Just Typical the last 2 C/D meetings between the two, but not by far. This reliable sort has the ability to turn the tables around this time out.
Price seems about right for this four-time CD winner for another stable. Not so good last time out, but can bounce back to win for the new stable, no problems. CD to suit.

Impeach drops back a furlong after being a beaten favourite here last time. He ran well for a long way before fading in the final furlong. The yard have hit top form in the last fortnight so there must be every chance that Joe Fanning's mount can go one better this time.

Big price here, but I'm willing to take an each-way chance. Progressive speed from the last run, and I liked the look of how Barney's Bay finished LTO 20/1 seems overpriced here. Joanna Mason in the saddle, and I think this horse is progressing slowly.

Love Rock looks like a lively one over this sharp five. She’s already shown she can win at the trip and wasn’t far away over six last time, so the drop back in distance could be bang on. She’s up a few pounds but still looks competitive and if she breaks well from the gates, she could be tough to peg back.
Most of these have major question marks, except this one who has had 3 runs to acquire a nice mark and now aims to win first time out in handicap company.
Not really sure why this is drifting, to be honest, as she looks to be well in based on her CD run three runs ago.

Midnightattheoasis is showing some promising signs. In his recent runs, he’s displayed a strong finishing kick and impressive stamina, which is a real asset on these Newcastle conditions. His consistency in similar races suggests he can be a solid bet, especially if he maintains his stride early and holds on in the final stages. The current price looks like good value given his form and track record, so I’m inclined to back him as a contender who could easily finish in the top positions.
Very consistent sort who gets the services of Billy here. Has been placing in most races of late and did win a few runs back. Well handicapped.

Pop Dancer went close last time when only beaten a length at Wolverhampton. He should go well for his first run at Newcastle. He hasn't won since 2023 and isn't getting any younger, but hopefully he will hit form again.

Henery Hawk hasn't won since Feb 24 after completing a double over C&D off marks of 54 & 63. The 6-year-old gelding has largely been out of form, dropping down in the ratings to 49 with winning jockey Tommie Jakes in the saddle taking off a useful 5 lbs. He hinted that he could be close to that elusive 5th win when 2nd, beaten 3/4 length to Shatin Venture over C&D 15 days ago. The Linda Perratt-owned and trained Heeraat gelding is the top-rated on the speed rating list, and the 3-time C&D winner must have a chance.

This is a trappy affair, and this trainer isn't prolific either. But Kipp Kelly caught my eye under this pilot, J Mason, when last seen here pulling hard and got the door shut, sending it right back where it got going again, finishing fastest of all. It may have been a flash in the pan, but I'll try an each way.

Sir Benedict is nothing special but is down to a mark where his connections will be told that he has a chance and will be trying to take it today. He has won 6 races in 5 years, but 3 of those wins have been in the last 12 months and ticks a few boxes here.

This is another Harbour Vision-Red Walls type bet from yesterday, which were both losers. But these seasoned campaigners are probably worth keeping onside at big prices as they've been there and done it and could pop in again. It's tricky to rule out ROCKLEY POINT based on his last handicap run at the beginning of the month. He has place claims if matching that performance.

Cloch Nua has been in great form recently, with a strong win at Newcastle that showcased his impressive stamina and ability to handle a demanding pace. He has consistently performed well on this track, and today’s conditions seem very favorable for his running style. His previous success here and solid finishing speed give me confidence in his potential to challenge the field effectively.

My vote here goes to the old boy Saisons D'or a three time course and distance winner who was last seen over this course and distance 24 days ago where finishing 6th/7 however he was returning from a 157 day break on the occasion and he did shape as if in need of the run now that the cob webs have been blown away Jedd O'Keeffe's inmate is likely to put up a bolder showing and can be a whole different proposition this time out currently operating on a mark of 62 he is more than capable of troubling the judge of this sort of mark jockey Jack Garrity takes the ride and can give Saisons D'or a promising ride here at Newcastle this looks a straightforward assignment for Saisons D'or and he merits serious consideration in a race of this nature

Bomb Squad's been running well since his win at Southwell. He's up a couple of pounds, but it shouldn't be too much of a problem. With P J McDonald in the saddle, that's a positive. He's been really consistent on the Tapeta lately, racking up a few wins. He should be there or thereabouts.
